File: scripts/slop_scan_local.py
Line: 23-28 HEREDOC_START_RE regex
Code: `\bpython3\b\n[^\n]*?\n(?P<operator><<-?)\n\s*\n(?P<quote>['"])\n(?P<tag>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\n(?P=quote)\n(?:\s+.*)?$`
Problem: The heredoc matcher allows trailing arbitrary shell operators/arguments on the opening line that immediately follow the tag quote, which can cause the closing tag to be missed if the shell operator injects whitespace or characters between the tag and heredoc start.
Why it fails at runtime: If a PR changed a shell script with a heredoc like `python3 - <<'PY' | cat`, the regex will still match but the body capture starts one line later after `python3 - <<'PY'` and any trailing operator, which can lead to incorrect line offset mapping for Python code inside the heredoc.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

File: scripts/slop_scan_local.py
Line: 401-445 _extract_python_heredoc_blocks
Code: Block capture uses `candidate = lines[cursor].lstrip("\t")` when allow_tabs is true, which strips leading tabs from heredoc body lines.
Problem: Shell linters treat heredocs as "here-documents and will-nohere" literals, so stripping leading tabs for shell scripts interferes with shell formatting and can break validation expectations.
Why it fails at runtime: For heredoc bodies in shell scripts, reliance on tabs is significant. This can cause the scanner to mis-align line numbers and affect the later `_scan_python_block` context, producing incorrect findings or line offsets.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

File: scripts/slop_scan_local.py
Line: 188 _try_node_types
Code: `return (ast.Try, try_star) if try_star is not None else (ast.Try,)`
Problem: No fallback for older Python versions ≤ 3.10 where `ast.TryStar` does not exist.
Why it fails at runtime: This may cause AttributeError when running on Python 3.9 or earlier CI runners.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/slop_scan_local.py
Line: 180-184 _is_docstring_expr
Code: Resilience to `ast.Constant` but direct access to `node.value` and `ast.Str` without guarding.
Problem: Forward compatibility: in AST of Python 3.12+, `ast.Str` is folded into `ast.Constant`. This can raise AttributeError or misclassify docstrings if AST traversers rely on the old node types in newer environments.
Why it fails at runtime: Compatibility issues when the environment runs under Python 3.12+. Under older Python, it still works via AST backward compat.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
